questions.passage: First, there is the pressure to be happy, which makes feeling sadness, anger, and anguish seem undesirable and alienating. And yet it is not possible to avoid negative emotions.
questions.prompt: Why does the author place “And yet” before the statement about negative emotions?
options: To show that unavoidable feelings conflict with the demand to be happy.
To deny that pressure changes how people view sadness.
To explain that criticism is less upsetting than missing a train.
To introduce the second face of the happiness trap in full.
analyses: A 对应 not possible to avoid 与前句 undesirable and alienating 的反差。
B yet 不是否定前面压力的影响，而是指出这种要求与情绪现实的冲突。
C 火车、批评、孩子不感恩是并列事例，没有程度排名。
D 此段标出 First 并继续解释第一面；第二面尚未在此完整展开。

evidence.quote: First, there is the pressure to be happy, which makes feeling sadness, anger, and anguish seem undesirable and alienating.
And yet it is not possible to avoid negative emotions.

vocabulary.meaning: 使疏离的；让人感到格格不入的
vocabulary.context: 快乐压力使负面感受显得不被接纳
vocabulary.example: The formal language can be alienating to new readers.

questions.translation: 首先，是必须幸福的压力，它使悲伤、愤怒和痛苦等感受显得不受欢迎，并让人感到格格不入。然而，负面情绪不可能完全避免。

questions.passage: For example, take an experience I had multiple times when I lived in New York City. I lived in a building without a door attendant. One day, when I came back to my building with some takeout food from the local Chinese restaurant, a young woman opened the door for me. So I said, “Thank you!”
questions.prompt: What kind of evidence is introduced by 'an experience I had multiple times'?
questions.promptZh: an experience I had multiple times 引入哪类材料？
options: A population survey of New York residents.
A first-person account of a repeated personal experience.
A story the advisor told the narrator about someone else.
An account of a single occasion with no suggestion of repetition.
optionsZh: 一项纽约居民总体调查。
反复发生过的个人经历的第一人称叙述。
导师告诉作者的他人故事。
一次单独事件的叙述，没有重复的意思。
analyses: A multiple times 指作者多次经历，不是居民调查样本。
B I had、when I lived in New York City 标明作者自己的经历，multiple times 说明不止一次。
C 本句说 I had，导师转述的故事属于后面另一段。
D multiple times 明确表示多次，不能删去次数限定。

vocabulary.context: 限定作者经历的次数，不能据此推出所有居民都经历相同事情。
vocabulary.example: She revised the paragraph multiple times before submitting it.

questions.translation: 例如，我住在纽约市时曾多次遇到这样的经历。我住的大楼没有门房。有一天，我从附近中餐馆买了外卖回楼里，一位年轻女子为我打开门，于是我说：“谢谢！”

evidence.quote: For example, take an experience I had multiple times when I lived in New York City.

questions.passage: For example, take an experience I had multiple times when I lived in New York City. I lived in a building without a door attendant. One day, when I came back to my building with some takeout food from the local Chinese restaurant, a young woman opened the door for me. So I said, “Thank you!”
questions.prompt: What detail is given about the building where the narrator lived?
questions.promptZh: 作者居住的大楼有什么特点？
options: It was staffed by several door attendants at all times.
It belonged to the Chinese restaurant.
It admitted only university professors.
It did not have a door attendant.
analyses: A without 与始终配备相反。
B 后文餐馆是外卖来源，没有产权关系。
C 作者的学术身份不能改成大楼的准入规定。
D without a door attendant 明确给出建筑的人员配置。

vocabulary.context: 指大楼门口的工作人员，without 说明该楼没有这项配置。
vocabulary.example: The visitor asked the door attendant for directions.
collocations: a building with a door attendant

questions.translation: 例如，我住在纽约市时曾多次遇到这样的经历。我住的大楼没有门房。有一天，我从附近中餐馆买了外卖回楼里，一位年轻女子为我打开门，于是我说：“谢谢！”

evidence.quote: I lived in a building without a door attendant.

questions.editorialStatus: 逐题作者稿；已核对实际PDF原页；定位到此前未直接配题的候选句，不改写原句、不把上下文当作直接证据。

questions.passage: When she replied, “Thank YOU!” I was completely thrown off. Then I realized: she assumed I was the Chinese deliveryman bringing her food.
questions.prompt: In the doorway anecdote, “completely thrown off” most nearly means that the author was:
options: physically prevented from entering his building.
confused by an unexpected response.
pleased to be recognised by a neighbour.
uncertain whether he had ordered the correct food.
analyses: A 把短语作字面动作理解；女子实际上给作者开了门。
B 对应出乎意料的回应以及随后才明白误会的时间顺序。
C 她把作者误认成送餐员，而非认出邻居；作者后来感到受辱。
D 没有怀疑自己点错餐的内容，误会涉及身份和食物去向。

evidence.quote: When she replied, “Thank YOU!” I was completely thrown off.
Then I realized: she assumed I was the Chinese deliveryman bringing her food.

vocabulary.context: 作者因对方反过来感谢他而一时困惑
vocabulary.example: The unexpected question threw me off.

vocabulary.context: 年轻女子误以为作者是给她送餐的人
vocabulary.example: I assumed the bag belonged to my neighbour.

questions.translation: 她却回答：“该谢谢你！”这让我完全摸不着头脑。随后我才明白，她以为我是给她送餐的中国外卖员。

questions.passage: Speaking of graduate school, when I was a fifth-year PhD student, my advisor told me the following story. Daniel Kahneman, a famous psychologist at Princeton, called my advisor, Ed Diener, up and asked him about me. At that time, there was an assistant professor job at Princeton that I had applied for. After they talked for a while, Kahneman asked my advisor, “Is Shige cocky?”
questions.prompt: At what stage of his studies did the advisor tell the narrator this story?
questions.promptZh: 导师是在作者学习生涯的哪个阶段告诉他这个故事的？
options: When he was a first-year PhD student.
After he had obtained his first professorship.
While applying to enter an undergraduate programme.
When he was a fifth-year PhD student.
optionsZh: 已获得第一个教授职位后。
analyses: A fifth-year 不是 first-year，学年被换错。
B 本句时间仍为博士学生阶段。
C PhD 与本科申请是不同阶段。
D when I was a fifth-year PhD student 直接给出时间。

vocabulary.context: 作者博士阶段的导师，后来在电话中向卡尼曼介绍作者。
vocabulary.example: Her advisor suggested a new direction for the thesis.

questions.translation: 说到研究生院，我读博士五年级时，导师给我讲了下面这个故事。普林斯顿的著名心理学家 Daniel Kahneman 打电话给我的导师 Ed Diener，向他打听我。当时，我申请了普林斯顿的一个助理教授职位。两人聊了一会儿后，Kahneman 问导师：“Shige 自负吗？”

evidence.quote: Speaking of graduate school, when I was a fifth-year PhD student, my advisor told me the following story.

questions.editorialStatus: 逐题作者稿；已核对实际PDF原页；定位到此前未直接配题的候选句，不改写原句、不把上下文当作直接证据。

questions.passage: A week later, I found out that I did not get the job interview at Princeton, while my “cocky” lab mate did!
questions.prompt: What outcome does the author explicitly report one week after the conversation?
options: His lab mate received an interview that he himself did not receive.
Kahneman interviewed him but rejected him after the meeting.
His lab mate accepted the Princeton job instead of him.
His advisor withdrew his application before Princeton considered it.
analyses: A 对应 did not get the job interview 与 lab mate did 的对照。
B 作者没有获得面试；不存在该段所说的面试后拒绝。
C 面试机会不等于录用或接受职位，结果范围被扩大。
D 导师谈及另一位学生，不等于正式撤回作者申请。

evidence.quote: A week later, I found out that I did not get the job interview at Princeton, while my “cocky” lab mate did!

vocabulary.context: 故事中 Kahneman 与导师讨论的一种性格
vocabulary.example: The player sounded confident without being cocky.

vocabulary.context: 对照作者没有获得面试与同门获得面试
vocabulary.example: Mia chose the train, while Leo drove.
